title: High school football roundup: Sumner tops Emerald Ridge, Enumclaw wins classic - NewsBreak
text:
By Tyler Wicke Jon Manley ,
21 hours ago Sumner tight end Gray Longoria (8) is pressured by Emerald Ridge defensive back Hunter Rusler (0) on Friday, Sept. 25, 2026, in Sumner, Wash. Liesbeth Powers/lpowers@thenewstribune.com Results, recaps and more from Week 4 high school football contests around the South Sound will be posted on this page Friday and Saturday. Looking for more scores? Find them on our statewide scoreboard here .
SATURDAY’S RESULTS (SEPT. 26)
Olympia running back Ibrahima Diallo (5) runs in a touchdown losing Capital's Carter Armstrong (4) on the way during the first half of the game at Ingersoll Stadium, on Friday, Sept. 4, 2026, in Olympia, Wash. Brian Hayes/bhayes@thenewstribune.com OLYMPIA 64, YELM 16 Ibrahima Diallo did it again.
Olympia’s top running back continued his breakout campaign with a 355-yard, six-touchdown performance in Saturday’s blowout win over Yelm.
Somehow, Diallo needed just eight carries to post video-game numbers, averaging 44.4 yards per tote. Through four games this fall, the 5-foot-9 senior has 73 carries for 960 yards and 13 touchdowns.
Head coach Cary Nagel’s Bears are undefeated (4-0) in his first year at the helm, set to continue their SPSL slate with Class 4A title contender Graham-Kapowsin on Oct. 2.
FRIDAY’S RESULTS (SEPT. 25)
SUMNER 24, EMERALD RIDGE 14 It’s been some time since an SPSL rival stole a win at Sunset Chev Stadium. 1,093 days, to be exact.
Ask head coach Keith Ross, and it’s been even longer since any team visiting the valley “wanted it more than us.”
It’s what Ross told his team in the locker room at halftime when Sumner trailed Emerald Ridge, 14-10, in a battle of unbeatens Friday night. The Spartans roster looks plenty different this fall, but that doesn’t change the inevitable: Everyone wants their shot at knocking off the back-to-back state champs.
“I didn’t get mad at them,” Ross said. “I just put it to them: ‘They want it more than you right now.’”
Sumner responded exactly how two-time defending Class 4A champions should.
Spartans defensive lineman Tyson Kukahiko promptly recovered a Jaguars fumble, dashing to the 4-yard line in the opening moments of the second half. That set up TE/DE Gray Longoria’s go-ahead touchdown catch.
When Emerald Ridge’s offense followed with a punt, Sumner delivered its heavyweight blow — a methodical, soul-crushing, 17-play drive capped by Santos Hernandez Ruiz’s eight-yard touchdown run. The Spartans never looked back in a 24-14 win.
Sumner running back Santos Hernandez Ruiz (22) carries the ball during a game against Emerald Ridge on Friday, Sept. 25, 2026, in Sumner, Wash. Liesbeth Powers/lpowers@thenewstribune.com “We knew we just needed to come out with way more juice than we entered with,” Longoria, a UNLV commit, told The News Tribune. “We did exactly that. Our guys got the job done.”
Emerald Ridge quarterback Brayden Paulino struck first, dashing to the right pylon for a four-yard touchdown run in the first quarter.
Sumner running back Von Jackson countered with a three-yard touchdown less than four minutes later.
Paulino found tight end Cody Dalton for a 14-yard touchdown in the second quarter. Sumner kicker Bergen Eriksson drilled a 24-yard field goal in the closing seconds of the half, cutting the Spartans’ deficit to four.
Longoria’s three-yard touchdown shortly after the break proved the game-winner.
“Just a simple cut right into the flat,” Longoria said. “They didn’t guard me, and it’s easy from there.”
Sumner (4-0) can extend its winning streak to 14 games (including the 2025 season) in a road matchup at Curtis on Oct. 2.
“We know we’re young, but we really just go out there with heart,” Longoria said. “We make sure we have elite physicality and effort, and that’s really our bread and butter.”
ENUMCLAW 28, FEDERAL WAY 27 The game had it all. Turnovers, momentum changes, big plays, long touchdown runs and even a dramatic, last-minute winning play.
“For some reason, it’s always like that when (Federal Way coach Marcus Yzaguirre) and I get together, you know,” Enumclaw coach Mark Gunderson said after Enumclaw’s 28-27 come-from-behind win.
Enumclaw forced and recovered a fumble late in the fourth quarter, giving the Hornets a final chance to win the game. On a third down from the Federal Way 12-yard line, Enumclaw quarterback Kannon Kuzaro softly lofted a pass into the waiting hands of Kortland Patterson. Enumclaw converted the PAT and held on for the 28-27 win.
“He put it on the spot, and I knew I wasn’t going to drop that,” Patterson said. “It was like a dream.”
Kuzaro wasn’t sure Enumclaw would get the ball back again in the fourth quarter. When the Hornets forced a fumble, he was ready to roll.
“I had to take a deep breath and be like, ‘I got another chance,’” Kuzaro said. “I just got to capitalize on it, and that’s what we did.”
Enumclaw running back Paxton Patterson single-handedly kept Enumclaw in the game in the first half while the Hornets’ offense sputtered. He rushed for 65-yard touchdown run just before halftime, then came through early in the third quarter with a 74-yard touchdown run.
“I think he’s the most underrated player in the state,” Kuzaro said. “Like, the fact he doesn’t have any D-I offers is ridiculous. His speed, size, it’s like he has to break one tackle and he’s gone. That’s what it is most of the time.”
Federal Way struck first on a 38-yard pass from Isaiah Healy to Kaicen Carter, who is star linebacker recruit. Tayven Collins added on with a 15-yard touchdown run, in which he broke several tackles en route to the end zone. Federal Way defensive end Micah Trumbo ripped the ball out of an Enumclaw running back’s hand and return it 75 yards for a score just before halftime, giving Enumclaw a 20-6 lead.
One of the game’s biggest moments was a blunder. The Federal Way long snapper sailed a toss over the punter’s head midway through the fourth quarter, bringing Enumclaw within six points. The Hornets took care of the rest.
The win, which all but locks up the 3A NPSL title for Enumclaw, came on the heels of a revenge win over rival White River a week earlier.
“These past two weeks were great,” Kuzaro said.
Federal Way should be fine. In addition to watching linebacker Kaicen Carter and safety Tayven Collins around, the Eagles return several players next week, after they sat out for four games, per the WIAA’s new transfer rules.
“We’ve got a lot of football to play and our best football is in front of us,” Yzaguirre said. “This is just a tough place to play. I’m super excited for what’s going to happen in the next couple weeks.”
PENINSULA 31, TIMBERLINE 14 Taking down crosstown-rival Gig Harbor in last weekend’s Fish Bowl is a tough act to follow, but the Peninsula Seahawks have delivered quite the encore.
Quarterback Talen McDonnell tossed three touchdown passes and the Seahawks knocked off undefeated Timberline, 31-14, in a statement win at South Sound Stadium (Lacey) on Friday night.
“A great team win,” Peninsula head coach Clay Mauro said. “Athletes were truly living our motto of 11 as 1. All the credit in the world to Timberline, a great program.
“Our boys came ready for a fourth-quarter battle, and played with discipline, physicality.”
McDonnell, also Peninsula’s kicker, drilled a 42-yard field goal before halftime that extended the lead to 10.
Seahawks receiver Jace Shanburn had six catches for 93 yards and a touchdown. WR/DB Landon Shultz caught three passes for 45 yards and two scores, adding eight tackles and an interception on defense.
Linebacker Thomas Marzano tallied 14 tackles (2 TFL) and forced a Timberline fumble. Defensive back Logan Johnson had two interceptions and five tackles.
Peninsula (2-2) hosts Capital in a 3A PSL matchup Oct. 2.
White River quarterback Chaz Strickland (7) prepares to throw the ball on Friday, Sept. 18, 2026, during the Battle of the Bridge rivalry game against Enumclaw in Buckley, Wash. Liesbeth Powers/lpowers@thenewstribune.com WHITE RIVER 54, THOMAS JEFFERSON 14 Hornets quarterback Chaz Strickland threw five touchdown passes and White River triggered the running clock before halftime in Friday night’s blowout win over Thomas Jefferson.
Senior receiver Parker Fry caught three of Strickland’s five touchdowns. It’s a promising rebound for White River following last weekend’s 28-14 loss to Enumclaw in the “Battle of the Bridge.”
“Nice bounce back after a tough Week 3 rivalry loss,” White River head coach Wyatt Evenson said. “Eight different players scored a TD and we were able to get our young players in mid-third quarter.”
White River (3-1) continues its 3A NPSL schedule in an Oct. 1 home matchup with Todd Beamer.
STADIUM 41, KENTRIDGE 21 Freshman quarterback Alex Richards’ three touchdown passes guided the Tigers to their first win of the season Friday night at Stadium Bowl.
Tigers receiver Odin Kalaua caught a pair of touchdowns and returned a kickoff for a third score. Stadium defensive tackle Kingsten Huston-McDuffie recorded seven tackles, a fumble recovery and a sack.
“Played sloppy football with lots of penalties,” Stadium head coach Patrick Johnson said. “However, a young team found a way to fight through a slow start and finished strong.”
Stadium visits Auburn Riverside in a 4A NPSL matchup Oct. 1.
BETHEL 21, BONNEY LAKE 12 Deron Williams’ 60-yard touchdown run in the fourth quarter sealed Bethel’s 21-12 win over Bonney Lake on Friday night.
Williams, a sophomore running back, finished with 180 yards and a pair of scores.
“(Bonney Lake) played super hard tonight,” Bethel head coach Travis Domser said. “It was nice for us to deal with adversity and still get the win.
“This is a tough league each week. No matter who you play, you better be ready.”
Bethel linebacker Elu Feo logged 10 tackles, two pass break-ups and a sack.
Bethel hosts Yelm in a 4A SPSL clash Oct. 2.
Mount Tahoma head coach Keith Terry looks on from the sidelines during the second half of the game at Yelm High School, on Thursday, Sept. 5, 2024, in Yelm, Wash. Brian Hayes/bhayes@thenewstribune.com MOUNT TAHOMA 28, SILAS 12 Mount Tahoma’s runaway third quarter lifted the T-Birds over Silas, 28-12, in Friday night’s Tacoma rivalry.
T-Birds receiver Jeremy Williams had four catches for 101 yards and a touchdown.
Mount Tahoma’s 3A PSL schedule continues at Bellarmine Prep on Oct. 2.
CASCADE CHRISTIAN 28, MONTESANO 27 Cascade Christian running back Donovan Walson erupted for 274 rushing yards and two touchdowns in Friday’s win over Montesano.
Walson, a two-way player and linebacker, added a sack on defense.
Cascade Christian (3-1) hosts Bellevue Christian on Oct. 3.
